To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
lidocaine selectively blocks the nociceptive transmission in the rat spinal cord.
the effect of lidocaine on the spinal cord is selective, i.e. it acts on the nociceptive transmission and does not affect the transmission of non-noxious information, and that it is transient.

the effect of systemically applied lidocaine on dorsal horn neurons is selective, i.e. it reduces or suppresses the responses to noxius stimuli whereas it has no effect on the responses to innocuous stimuli and the spontaneous activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new drugs for the treatment of neuropathic pain and with the study of the mechanisms of action of these drugs.
the study of the effect of lidocaine on nociceptive and non nociceptive transmission in the spinal cord.
the study of the mechanisms underlying nociception and pain, and with the development of novel analgesic agents, based on the inhibition of the activity of nociceptive neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
lidocaine is a selective inhibitor of the transmission of the nociceptive input at the spinal level.

the spinal cord is a target for lidocaine, and that the drug is able to exert a selective inhibitory action on nociceptive information transmission at this level, without affecting the transmission of non-noxious inputs.

lidocaine, in addition to its local anaesthetic effect, exerts a systemic analgesic action which can be explained on the basis of a selective inhibition of noxious stimuli transmission in the central nervous system, probably at the level of the dorsal horn.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lidocaine, in the dose range of 2-4 mg kg(-1), selectively inhibits the nociceptive transmission without affecting other sensory modalities.

lidocaine acts on the nociceptive transmission in the dorsal horn of the spinal cord and this effect is mediated by an interaction of lidocaine with sodium channels in the nociceptive afferent terminals.
lidocaine acts as a specific inhibitor of nociceptive transmission in the dorsal horn.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lidocaine has a selective inhibitory action on noxious stimuli.
lidocaine is a potent inhibitor of noxious-evoked activity in the spinal cord.
lidocaine has a selective action on the nociceptive pathway.
